newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ymos expects decision on sale by September.
newsitem.headline: Ymos expects decision on sale by September.

text.p: Ymos AG Chairman Klaus Troester said on Tuesday he expected the company's largest shareholder, steel maker Cockerill Sambre SA, to decide by September on a possible sale of its shares.
Belgian group Cockerill owns 95 percent of the German car parts maker and has said in the past that it wanted to end its involvement in the auto business.
Troester said, however, he did not expect the company's share price to collapse if Cockerill goes ahead with the sale. "A short-term share crash is not to be expected," he said.
Cockerill bought Ymos in February 1989 when the original owners of the company, the Becker and Wolf families, were unable to provide the company with sufficient capital.
Ymos shares last traded at 103.10 marks on Monday. No shares had been traded by mid-afternoon on Tuesday.
